title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-13
content:
Notes / scratchpad (personal) - throughput regression after weekend deploy

Summary:
- Observed a ~30-40% drop in overall throughput (tokens/s) for medium-length chat workloads after the 2026-02-24 deploy (commit abc123).
- p50 latency stable, but p95/p99 spiked and tail latency increased; throughput dropped under identical QPS.
- Hypothesis: continuous batching got effectively disabled or misconfigured, causing more synchronous/gang scheduling and losing batching efficiency. Also investigating KV cache/TTL interactions.

Quick timeline:
- 2026-02-24 03:20 UTC: deploy abc123 (PR #456 merged)
- 2026-02-24 04:05 UTC: first uptick in p99 latency; Sentry alerts for >200ms tail
- 2026-02-24 04:30 UTC: ops oncall: temporarily scaled dedicated pool up +10% (no real improvement)
- 2026-02-24 05:00 UTC: rolled back model variant to v1.3.2 -> no improvement
- 2026-02-24 06:15 UTC: discovered config-map value for continuous_batching.enabled=false in model-config-map (see evidence below)

Commands I ran (notes + outputs):
- Check config seen by runtime (inside a sample pod):
  kubectl exec -it pod/serve-abc-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'jq .continuous_batching /etc/model-config.json'
  OUTPUT: false

- Inspect config map created by deploy job:
  kubectl get configmap model-config-xyz -o yaml | sed -n '1,120p'
  OUTPUT snippet: continuous_batching:
    enabled: false
    max_batch_size: 64
    batch_timeout_ms: 8

- Confirm runtime log lines during request handling (tail):
  [2026-02-24T04:29:58Z] INFO serve: request queued, batching_key=chat_v1 user=acct-77 queue_len=2
  [2026-02-24T04:29:58Z] WARN serve: continuous batching disabled by config, falling back to immediate dispatch

- Metrics (prometheus query, 2026-02-24 04:00-06:00 UTC):
  sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[5m])) by (pod) dropped from ~120k -> ~75k tokens/s for pool 'dedicated-medium'
  serve_batch_size_avg{pool="dedicated-medium"} decreased from 18 -> 6

- Repro attempt (local dev env with test harness):
  ./run_e2e.sh --model chat_v1 --qps 40 --len 120 --duration 10m
  Observed: average batch size 5-7, end-to-end throughput ~60% of baseline.

Error / interesting logs:
- "continuous batching disabled by config, falling back to immediate dispatch" (multiple pods)
- "batch_queue_max_size reached, rejecting new request" (rare, correlated with request bursts)
- KV-cache hits didn't change materially (hit_rate ~0.72 -> 0.69) but cache TTL in config is 0s in the applied config-map (suspicious)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Config drift: PR #456 unintentionally changed default for continuous_batching.enabled to false (see PR diff). The deploy's config-generation job wrote a configmap with enabled:false. Evidence: configmap value and runtime logs. Likelihood: high.
2) Batching algorithm fallback: recent kernel selection changes in serving runtime cause the continuous batching path to hit a guard and forcibly disable (safety) under certain tokenization patterns. Evidence: runtime logs include guard-level warnings in same window. Likelihood: medium.
3) KV cache TTL set to 0 cause many cache misses and higher work per request, reducing effective batching (longer per-request processing reduces opportunity to batch). Evidence: configmap TTL=0 and slight drop in hit rate. Likelihood: low-medium.
4) Autoscaler/placement change: pods getting less co-location for batching keys, causing smaller batches. Check scheduler events. Likelihood: low.

Evidence supporting config drift:
- git history: PR #456 (serving-runtime) modifies default config generation -> default continuous_batching.enabled=false.
- Configmap from prod shows enabled:false and TTL=0.
- Runtime logs explicitly say "disabled by config".
- Repro locally when starting runtime with that config results in same throughput drop.

Immediate mitigation (short-term):
- Patch configmap in prod to set continuous_batching.enabled=true and reasonable defaults: max_batch_size: 128, batch_timeout_ms: 12, kv_cache_ttl_s: 3600.
- Roll restart the serving pods in pool 'dedicated-medium' (orderly, one at a time).
- Monitor batch_size_avg and tokens/s during roll.

Commands to apply patch quickly (tested on staging):
- kubectl patch configmap model-config-xyz -p '{"data":{"continuous_batching.enabled":"true","continuous_batching.max_batch_size":"128","continuous_batching.batch_timeout_ms":"12","kv_cache.ttl_s":"3600"}}' || true
- kubectl rollout restart statefulset/serve-dedicated-medium -n inference || true

Longer-term fixes / PR actions:
- Revert PR #456 default change or make generator respect existing cluster override (need a gate).
- Add CI check: ensure config generator doesn't flip continuous batching without an explicit flag in release notes.
- Add runtime metric: continuous_batching.active{pod=} gauge + alert if zero across pool during normal operation.
- Add end-to-end test in perf CI that validates average batch size doesn't drop by >20% after deploy in a representative workload.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Was there another deploy (infra) at the same time that could have touched scheduler/pod placement? Check release-engineering logs (ask Lisa).
- Where is the config generator code? Confirm location and rollback plan. (linked: PR #456)
- Are there any operator overrides (SRE automation) that could have applied a different configmap post-deploy? Check automation logs.

Notes-to-self for post-mortem:
- Capture exact configmap diffs and time series of batch_size_avg, tokens/s, p99 latency for 48h window around deploy.
- Interview oncall and release owner for deploy abc123.
- Draft blameless postmortem and remediation, include checklist for config generator releases.

Quick reproduction checklist (for others):
1) Checkout PR #456 diff locally
2) Generate config artifact with generator: ./config-gen --model chat_v1 --output tmp.json
3) Start runtime locally with tmp.json and run e2e harness (./run_e2e.sh)
4) Observe batch_size metrics via /metrics endpoint and local grafana dashboard

Anchors / refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456 (default config change)
- Jira: JIRA-2026 (incident ticket)
- Slack channel thread: #serving-runtime (link above)

Next actions (me):
- Patch configmap in prod (today) and restart pods -> monitor for improvement (Matt to help)
- Prepare rollback of PR #456 or a follow-up PR to re-enable default and add tests (Diego to review)
- Write perf CI check (follow-up ticket)

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Could add a runtime safety: if batch_size_avg drops 50% relative to baseline and continuous_batching.enabled==false, emit high-severity alert: possible misconfig/deploy.
- Consider storing recent config checksum in metrics so we can quickly correlate config changes to perf drops.

-- Aisha
